Identity.History:
Gorgidas was a prominent Theban general of the early 4th century BC, best known for his role in rebuilding Thebes as a major military power after the city threw off Spartan domination in 379 BC. He is traditionally credited with organizing the Sacred Band of Thebes, an elite corps of 300 hoplites whose discipline and cohesion helped transform the Theban army. Gorgidas initially appears to have distributed these men among the regular battle line as a stiffening force, before the unit was later concentrated into a single formation under Pelopidas.
He was also active in the fighting that followed Thebes’ liberation, helping defend Boeotia against repeated Spartan invasions and contributing to the military reforms that preceded the great Theban victories of the 370s and 360s BC. Although later overshadowed by Pelopidas and Epaminondas, Gorgidas belongs to the generation of commanders who laid the foundations for Thebes’ brief rise to supremacy in Greece.
